data.title: Chinese Tesla Suppliers Pare Gains After Denying Knowledge of Optimus Factory Checks
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 18 -- Shares of Tesla’s Chinese suppliers such as Tuopu Group and Sanhua Intelligent Controls retreated from intraday highs after the firms said they had no knowledge of factory inspections in China tied to the US firm’s Optimus humanoid robot, following a report that a Tesla team arrived in Ningbo this week to assess suppliers ahead of mass production.

After climbing by almost 7 percent in Shanghai this morning, Tuopu [SHA: 601689] closed up 2.8 percent at CNY45 (USD6.71) per share. Sanhua [SHE: 002050] retreated from an earlier gain of 4.3 percent to finish 1.9 percent higher at CNY35.31 (USD5.27).

Tuopu has not received any notification about a facility inspection by Tesla, a representative for the Ningbo-based company told Yicai. The pair have collaborated on linear and rotary actuators as well as dexterous hand actuators, the person said, adding that the production base for these components is ready.

A Sanhua representative said the Shaoxing-based manufacturer was not aware of Tesla's new round of facility inspections, but did confirm that it is working with a major client on developing robot joint actuators.

According to a report published yesterday by 21st Century Business Herald, a Tesla inspection team arrived in Ningbo on Sept. 16 to check the facilities of potential suppliers as the Austin-based company prepares to begin mass production of its Optimus robot. Tesla has already issued orders to various suppliers, the report said.


“Tesla's R&D personnel are typically present at the factory in Ningbo, which handles both auto and robotics businesses,” the Tuopu representative pointed out.

Previous reports had said that Tesla launched a round of robotics facility inspections in China last September, involving some of its already established automotive supply chain partners, such as Tuopu, Sanhua, Xinquan Automotive Trim, and Joyson Electronics.

A Joyson representative declined to comment on the matter today, citing client confidentiality. After gaining by as much as 5.6 percent in morning trading, Joyson’s stock price [SHA: 600699] ended 1.4 percent higher at CNY20.14 (USD3).

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: Alibaba’s DAMO Academy Debuts Generalist AI for Nearly 150 Abdominal Conditions
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 18 -- Alibaba Group Holding’s DAMO Academy has unveiled an artificial intelligence model that can identify nearly 150 abdominal conditions, such as stomach and liver cancers, potentially replacing multiple disease-specific models with a single system.

The pioneering model, known as DAMO RADAR, has been open-sourced and covers a broad range of abdominal findings, including malignant tumors, the Hangzhou-based research institute said today. The findings were published in Science.

Founded by the Chinese e-commerce giant in 2017, DAMO Academy conducts research into AI and other emerging technologies. Its achievements include the Tongyi family of AI models, XuanTie processors and Hanguang 800 AI chip, as well as AI systems for detecting cancers.

DAMO RADAR could transform the detection of conditions such as pancreatic cancer, fatty liver disease, and acute appendicitis. The academy said that abdominal CT scans are among the most complex medical images, while existing AI models typically target individual diseases and struggle with broader clinical needs.

To overcome the challenge, the team used vision-language learning to link medical images with reports and identify a broad range of clinical findings. The team also converted CT images into three-dimensional anatomical units, precisely aligning them with medical reports to improve performance.

Researchers evaluated DAMO RADAR on 146 clinical findings involving 18 anatomical structures, with the model achieving a mean area under the curve (AUC) of 0.913 across nearly 40,000 real-world examinations. AUC measures how well a model distinguishes between positive and negative cases, with a score of one indicating perfect performance.

The research team also compared the model with 26 radiologists, with the model’s average performance exceeding that of 23 of them. The study also showed that DAMO RADAR could help radiologists increase disease-detection sensitivity by 10 percent while reducing the time needed by 30 percent.

DAMO RADAR has strong generalization capabilities and broad applicability, said Zhang Ling, a senior algorithm expert at DAMO Academy. The research approach could potentially be extended beyond identifying multiple findings in abdominal CT scans to other forms of medical imaging, accelerating the development of artificial general intelligence, he added.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: China’s Eve Energy Surges After Unit Inks Major Deal to Supply Batteries to Fluence Energy
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 18 -- Eve Energy's stock price soared after the Chinese lithium battery maker said a subsidiary has secured a major five-year order to supply batteries to Fluence Energy Global Production Operation, a Nasdaq-listed energy storage products and services giant.

After surging by as much as 7.9 percent in Shenzhen trading this afternoon, Eve Energy [SHE: 300014] finished 6.9 percent higher at CNY51.56 (USD7.70) per share. The stock is still down about 25 percent this year.

Hubei Eve Power, a wholly owned subsidiary, has contracted to deliver 16 gigawatt-hours of energy storage batteries to Fluence Energy next year and reserve another 190 GWh for handover in 2028 to 2031, its Huizhou-based parent company announced today, without providing further details.

Founded in 2001 as a lithium-ion battery manufacturer, Eve Energy has grown into a top-tier global supplier for electric vehicles and become one of the world’s leading producers of stationary, utility-scale energy storage units. Last year, the company shipped 71.05 GWh of energy storage batteries and 50.15 GWh of power batteries.

The Fluence Energy deal demonstrates that Eve Energy's battery performance and supply capabilities have been reorganized by international energy storage product integrators, the company said. It will also help to establish a long-term strategic alliance between the two parties, Eve said, adding that the firm will continue to consolidate and enhance its influence and competitiveness in the global new energy market. 

Virginia-based Fluence Energy is a Tier 1 grid-level battery energy storage system integrator jointly formed by US utility and power generation firm AES and German industrial behemoth Siemens. Its global production and operations unit oversees manufacturing and delivery of energy storage equipment, as well as the operation and maintenance of power stations.

Hubei Eve Power is one of the two local operators that run Eve Energy’s battery production base in Jingmen, central Hubei province. The facilities under Hubei Eve Power turn out power batteries as well as energy storage cells, which are mainly used in commercial and industrial settings, alongside grid-side and telecom backup applications.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: China’s Zangge, Yuntu to Spend USD171 Million for Control of Congo Potash Miner
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 18 -- China’s Zangge Mining and Yuntu Holdings said they plan to jointly spend USD171 million to take control of Kanga Potash, which is developing a pre-production Kanga potash mine in the Republic of the Congo, with the aim of increasing their access to high-quality potash.

Zangge and Yuntu intend to set up a joint venture in Singapore, with the former indirectly holding a 75 percent stake and the latter indirectly owning the rest, to fund and acquire 92 percent of Kanga Potash, the pair announced separately late yesterday. Sarmin Group, an existing shareholder of the target company, will keep the remaining 8 percent.

Registered in Mauritius, Kanga Potash's key assets include the mining permit for the Kanga potash mine and exploration rights for the Loango potash block in Congo, Zangge and Yuntu pointed out. It posted a net loss of USD1.7 million in the eight months ended Aug. 31, they added.

Zangge’s stock price [SHE: 000408] closed 1.7 percent higher at CNY72.16 (USD10.77) in Shenzhen today, while Yuntu [SHE: 002539] added 0.6 percent to end at CNY12.31 (USD1.84).

The Kanga mining permit covers a 321-square-kilometer area and is valid though June 2047. Kanga Potash also secured a 25-year mining convention with the Congolese government in August 2023, the firms said.

Under the permit, the deposit contains 810 million tons of measured potassium chloride resources with an average grade of 17.1 percent, plus 1.18 billion tons of inferred resources at a 16.5 percent grade. Total resources amount to two billion tons at an average grade of 16.7 percent.

Potash is a group of potassium-containing minerals and salts, which is mainly used as an agricultural fertilizer.

Zangge will indirectly control the target assets and act as the lead on the Kanga potash mine, the Golmud-based company said, adding that it will push forward pre-construction work, complete all regulatory approvals, and aim to start construction and commissioning early.

The acquisition will expand Yuntu's potash resources base, address a key gap in its upstream potash portfolio, and enhance long-term security of supply for a critical fertilizer raw material, according to the phosphate miner, which is also one of China's leading compound fertilizer makers.

 

Zangge Mining specializes in developing salt-lake mineral resources and is controlled by Zijin Mining, one of China's largest mining companies. Chengdu-based Yuntu as multiple phosphate mining rights and phosphate exploration permits.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: China’s Yitoa Rises on Plan to Obtain 15-Year Global Manufacturing, Sales License for Three Car Display Chips From Synaptics
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 18 -- Shares of Yitoa Intelligent Control jumped after the Chinese electronic component distributor said it plans to secure a 15-year global exclusive manufacturing and sales license for three types of vehicle display chips from Nasdaq-listed mixed-signal semiconductor solutions supplier Synaptics Incorporated.

Yitoa [SHE: 300131] closed 2 percent higher at CNY16.15 (USD2.41) a share today, after earlier rising by as much as 4 percent. The broader Shenzhen market climbed 1.7 percent.

Yitoa and some of its consolidated subsidiaries will sign a licensing agreement with Synaptics to obtain the rights for part of its display driver integrated circuits, touch and display driver integration chips, and smart bridge-specific chips and solutions for intelligent cockpit displays, as well as relevant derivative products, the Shenzhen-based company said in a stock exchange filing late yesterday.

Under the agreement, Synaptics will receive a payment of USD20 million in three installments from Yitoa, as well as quarterly royalties based on net sales, the Chinese company said. However, some licensed chips cannot be sold to Chinese mainland customers, it added, without disclosing which products are restricted or why.

DDIC chips are used in non-touch car displays, TDDI chips are mainly used for touch-enabled large screens for central vehicle control and entertainment, and smart bridge chips split and distribute complete image signals across multiple adjacent display panels. The multi- and large-screen trend in car cockpits has boosted demand for all three.

The licensed products are mature chips, with peak sales period for existing inventory projects estimated to last about three to four years, according to Yitoa. By inheriting Synaptics’ customers, the partnership will help the Chinese firm gain faster access to the supply chains of leading global automakers and markedly shorten the time frame for the business to reach its harvest season, it added.

In addition, the deal will help Yitoa scale up procurement, boosting its bargaining power with upstream wafer fabs, packaging and test houses, and third-party intellectual property vendors, which will in turn cut development and manufacturing costs for its own proprietary display chips and accelerate mass production rollout, it pointed out.

California-based Synaptics is a leading global supplier of custom human-machine interface solutions. Its products are used in smartphones, tablets, personal computers, and other electronic devices, including car displays.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: DeepSeek Engineer Says AI May Soon Outstrip His Abilities
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 16 -- Shengyu Liu, who developed a core component of DeepSeek’s newly released V4.1 artificial intelligence model, expects AI to catch up with and possibly surpass the quality of his own work in a matter of months, highlighting how AI is moving beyond routine software tasks and into the specialized engineering work that powers the technology itself.

Liu, a machine learning systems engineer at the Hangzhou-based AI unicorn, said in an article posted on his personal WeChat account recently that he probably will not become unemployed because of AI, but he may well be forced to "change professions.”

Liu was a member of Peking University’s 2021 Turing Class, an elite undergraduate cohort in computer science, and previously captained the university’s supercomputing team, leading it to top-two finishes in international university supercomputing competitions.

Just days ago, Liu completed the main attention operator for DeepSeek’s V4.1, a core component that determines the model’s inference efficiency. But within six months to a year, AI-written operators will probably match or even outstrip his own abilities, he admitted.

Liu expects that he may eventually have to give up the operator design and manual optimization he loves to become a “mech pilot” of AI agents, directing models, breaking down tasks, evaluating results, and taking responsibility for the final system.

Liu described the shift as a “technological paradox.” “The better operators I write, the faster our new models train and run inference, and the more rapidly model capabilities advance, meaning I get replaced sooner,” Liu pointed out.

“AI can think of 300 tokens in one second, write a command in half a second, and finish writing code in 20 seconds, which I can’t," Liu said.

Unlike humans, AI can also continue to scale its reasoning, tool use, and ability to perform tasks in parallel, he said. It has evolved from an assistant that merely searches documentation and reads code into one capable of independently analyzing and optimizing operators using Compute Unified Device Architecture, Nvidia’s programming platform for graphics processing units, Liu said.

Liu’s concern reflect a broader shift as AI programming tools become embedded in developers’ daily work. According to the 2026 Developer Survey report released by code quality platform Sonar, 72 percent of developers who have used AI programming tools use them every day, while 42 percent of code submitted by respondents is AI-generated or heavily AI-assisted, up from just 6 percent in 2023.

AI is also changing the skills employers look for in programmers, according to the China Software Industry Association. At a press conference held by China’s industry and information technology ministry last week, CSIA Secretary-General Lv Weifeng addressed the debate over whether AI will replace programmers.

Pure coding skills will become less important, while understanding requirements, designing architectures, integrating systems, and ensuring quality and safety will become more important, he said. Lv added that collaborating with AI is becoming a core skill for programmers, requiring them to clearly communicate tasks, evaluate AI-generated output, and coordinate multiple AI agents.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: China’s Fulongma Soars by Limit on Tie-Up With Huawei on Self-Driving Tech for Sanitation Vehicles
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 18 -- Shares of Fulongma Group surged by the exchange-imposed daily trading limit after the leading Chinese supplier of environmental sanitation equipment announced a partnership with Huawei Technologies to develop autonomous driving technologies for sanitation vehicles.

Fulongma [SHA: 603686] closed up 10 percent at CNY15.47 (USD2.30) in Shanghai today.

Huawei Cloud Computing Technology will exclusively develop and deploy a self-driving system for sanitation vehicles for Fulongma for CNY200 million (USD29.9 million), the Longyan-based firm announced yesterday, citing a three-year technical service contract. The system will include cloud-based and vehicle-end software, as well as intelligent hardware solutions.

The partnership, which also involves technical development and research on intelligent transformations, drive-by-wire optimizations, and cloud adaptations, aims to expand the use of autonomous driving technology in Fulongma’s sanitation vehicle products and strengthen its digital and intelligent capabilities.

Building on this foundation, Huawei Cloud will lead the adaptation and validation of self-driving algorithm software for Fulongma's three- and six-ton payload sanitation vehicle models for sweeping and washing scenarios. This will enable a closed-loop data link, allowing for model algorithms to be incrementally trained and continuously iterated.

Huawei Cloud will also help Fulongma enhance its research and development capabilities for autonomous driving solutions, preparing for the technical and operational integration needed to commercialize unmanned sanitation vehicles in the future.

This collaboration does not involve the transfer of technology. The partnership results will grant Fulongma a non-exclusive, general-use license from Huawei, which cannot be sublicensed or redistributed. Fulongma will not be required to pay additional licensing fees to use the R&D results.

Huawei will own the models obtained through incremental training on Fulongma's data. Fulongma will be able to access the results by subscribing to Huawei Cloud's public cloud sanitation autonomous driving services.

This exclusive technical collaboration is an important strategic initiative for Fulongma's intelligent upgrade of its sanitation equipment business, the firm noted.

By leveraging the respective industrial advantages of the two parties, Fulongma will rapidly enhance its end-to-end autonomous sanitation driving system capabilities, leading to the launch of unmanned sanitation equipment products with advanced autonomous driving features. This, in turn, will improve the core competitiveness and differentiation advantages of the company's products.

This collaboration will also establish a joint R&D and joint marketing assurance mechanism. While accelerating technology iteration and product implementation, the two firms will work together to expand the smart sanitation equipment market.

Fulongma previously attempted to develop unmanned sanitation products and achieved demonstration operations and small-scale commercial sales. Its sales revenue from this business reached CNY9.9 million (USD1.5 million) last year and nearly CNY5 million (USD738,880) in the first half of this year.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: Hainan’s First Hualong One Nuclear Power Unit Enters Commercial Operation
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 18 -- China National Nuclear Corporation and China Huaneng Group, two major state-owned atomic energy developers, have put the first Hualong One nuclear power unit in China’s southernmost Hainan province into operation.

Unit 3 of the Changjiang nuclear power plant, the first of the project’s second phase, has officially entered the commissioning phase, providing reliable clean energy support for the island as it develops into a free trade port, Hainan announced on its official WeChat account yesterday.

The second phase of the Changjiang nuclear power plant is Hainan's largest power engineering construction project, comprising two Hualong One atomic units with an installed capacity of 1.2 million kilowatts each. Once fully operational, its total annual power output will reach 18 billion kW-hours, equivalent to reducing standard coal consumption by 6.3 million tons and carbon dioxide emissions by 11.6 million tons.

The first two units of the Changjiang nuclear power plant were put into commercial operation in December 2015 and August 2016, respectively. Atomic power accounted for nearly 19 percent of Hainan’s total electricity generation last year, according to data from the National Energy Administration.

Last December, Hainan became the Chinese mainland's first FTP and the world's largest FTP by area. According to a national strategic plan, Hainan will leverage its FTP policies to develop tourism, modern service industries, and high-tech industries, aiming to establish itself as an international tourism and consumption center and a model zone for ecological civilization.

While building itself into a high-level FTP, Hainan will also accelerate its green energy transition. The proportion of non-fossil energy to the province’s total energy consumption is expected to increase to 35 percent by 2030 from 21 percent in 2024, achieving the carbon peak target as planned, according to a plan released by the provincial government in June.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Futura Costaglione

data.title: China Nerin Pens USD498 Million EPC Deal for Copper Tailings Treatment Plant in Zambia
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 18 -- Nerin Engineering, the leading non-ferrous metal engineering technology service provider in China, said it secured a USD498 million engineering, procurement, and construction contract for a copper tailings treatment factory in Zambia.

 Nerin will build the plant with an annual capacity of 70,000 tons for Konkola Copper Mines in Chingola, the Nanchang-based company announced late yesterday. The facility will help the client efficiently recover valuable metals from its existing copper tailings and improve the comprehensive utilization rate of its resources, it noted. 

Under the EPC contract, Nerin will handle project design and equipment procurement, construction, installation, and debugging, as well as provide technical support and employee training services, it noted, without disclosing when construction will start or how long it will take. KCM will pay for the project according to agreed milestones and other arrangements, it added.

 The deal will help Nerin gain experience in high-end overseas projects and localized operations, enhance its overseas general contracting engineering capabilities, boost its global brand influence, and positively impact its business performance, according to the company.

 Nerin provides domestic and foreign non-ferrous metal customers with full-chain technical solutions and end-to-end services, including mining, beneficiation, smelting, and processing. Its overseas revenue topped CNY502.9 million (USD75.1 million) in the first half of this year, accounting for 73 percent of its total income, and it signed five engineering service deals, including mining, processing, and tailings treatment, in the period, according to its financial report.

Shares of Nerin [SHA: 603257] dropped 3 percent to CNY68.29 (USD10.18) each as of 2.20 p.m. Shanghai today, after opening up 4.4 percent.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: New Generation Is Transforming China's Family Businesses
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 18 -- Judy Chan joined her family's business in 2002 at the age of 24, when her father asked her over dinner whether she wanted to take charge of bottling and packaging at his wine company despite her having just started work at US investment bank Goldman Sachs and not knowing anything about what type of business he was running, as she had never even seen him drink wine.

More than two decades later, Chan has turned the business into one of China's better-known boutique wineries, Grace Vineyard in Shanxi province. The company has expanded into whisky production in her ancestral Fujian province and has brought in an outside majority shareholder.

Chan's experience is part of a broader generational transition in Chinese family businesses, many of which were founded during the reform era of the 1980s and 1990s and are now being passed to a new generation for the first time, inheriting capital but facing a different market environment than their parents.

Succession involves more than transferring ownership - it requires a commitment to intergenerational stewardship, Chan and several family business figures said in interviews with Yicai. It can also involve changes in decision-making, risk tolerance, and the role family capital plays across generations, they pointed out.

Founders who built businesses during periods of rapid economic growth often maintained centralized control, an approach that can create challenges when responsibility is transferred to the next generation.

"Founders who can manage thousands of employees sometimes find it challenging to manage family dynamics," said Zhang Yong, founder and chairman of Deyu Family Office.

What matters is not this year's profit but "whether what I leave the next generation strengthens or burdens them," said Bernard Chan, chairman of Asia Financial Holdings, adding that this includes not only financial assets but also organizational practices and unresolved risks.

Judy Chan said her father took a relatively hands-off approach when she moved into the business, often advising her to use her university degree and not make a mistake she cannot undo. She recalled deciding whether to import French bottles at 10 times the price of domestic ones, not knowing whether the potential effect on product and sales could justify the higher cost. "Making the call is genuinely difficult as you don't know if turning left or right is correct. Both are possible."

Chavalit Frederick Tsao, chairman of four-generation multinational firm TPC (Tsao Pao Chee), said that his children were raised overseas, but the family's values could still be passed on. "What matters is whether you've actually lived out the values yourself. Explaining doesn't work, but demonstrating does."

Formal education increasingly transmits knowledge that artificial intelligence can replicate certain types of knowledge, while values, judgment, and restraint depend more on personal experience and example, Tsao stressed.

Different Market for the Next Generation

Many Chinese businesses established during the 1980s and 1990s expanded into multiple sectors as new opportunities emerged, including coal exports, department stores, and wastewater treatment.

The environment facing younger business operators is different, Chan said. "The environment facing younger business operators is different, with a more competitive landscape."

For example, China's wine sector has grown from a few dozen recognizable domestic labels to more than 1,000 competing brands, she pointed out, noting that the market is also no longer expanding at the pace seen in earlier years. The change has meant placing greater emphasis on cost control and cash flow, with Grace Vineyard maintaining a policy of not extending credit terms to buyers, she said.

"The day cash isn't in the bank, sales are notional, and chasing payment consumes disproportionate time," she stressed. Grace Vineyard has also shifted some attention from wholesale channels toward direct-to-consumer experiences at its winery.

In an AI-enabled business environment, companies can increasingly operate with "low organizational density but high individual leverage," with smaller teams using technology to achieve tasks that previously required larger workforces, enabling more agile operations, said Johnny Zou, founder of Honghub, China’s first accelerator community dedicated to “one-person companies”.

Turning Purpose Into Capital Structure

Terms such as "patient capital," "regenerative capital," and "love as infrastructure" have featured prominently at family capital gatherings this year. Some participants have also sought to translate these ideas into specific financing models.

Asked whether values-based investing is too abstract to understand, Chairman Tsao said that Chinese philosophical traditions should be understood as a practical "discipline of living" rather than as ideas separate from everyday action. He outlined a potential financing model for ocean and climate restoration projects, where funding needs can reach trillions of dollars a year and commercial returns may initially be limited.

Philanthropic capital can provide early funding and absorb higher risks while projects develop their initial business models. Once a model shows returns of around 7 percent, impact-investment funds can participate. As projects scale and returns move into double digits, private equity and eventually larger institutional investors may become potential sources of capital.

Green investment can be linked to commercial value when a company addresses a specific customer need, according to Zhang Guojin, co-founder of Asia Green Fund and CEO of Asia Green Fund Management. For example, the products of a reusable-packaging company lowered customers' logistics costs while also reducing material waste, he added.

"Purpose should be a source of returns, not something balanced against them," Zhang stressed.

People in their twenties and thirties can focus on "financial ambition," while by their forties they can begin establishing "moral ambition," rather than waiting until later in life to consider how they want to contribute to society, James Chen, chairman of the Chen Yet-Sen Family Foundation.

Ownership Without Inheritance

For many family businesses, maintaining family ownership has traditionally been an important part of succession, but Chan took a different approach at Grace Vineyard, reducing her stake and bringing in an outside majority shareholder while remaining involved in product and brand development.

"People ask if I intend to hand this to my children. I never thought of it that way," she said. "I'd like the brand to survive, for people to remember what we built. That, to me, is what matters most."

A separate project has also connected Chan's business activities with her family history. She built a whisky distillery in Fujian's Longyan, a region her grandfather and great-grandfather left as teenagers when they emigrated to Southeast Asia, holding the groundbreaking ceremony on her grandfather's birthday.

Whisky requires years of aging before it can be sold, giving the project a long production cycle, Chan pointed out, noting that the process reflects her family history that spans several generations, from migration to Southeast Asia to winemaking in Shanxi and, eventually, whisky production in Fujian.

Finding Common Ground

Patience emerged as one recurring theme in discussions of family business succession and long-term investment.

"You can't force time," Chan said, recalling her early desire to master legal, negotiation, and other business skills as quickly as possible. "Looking back, moving slowly usually gets you further than trying to leap ahead. Give yourself time and give your parents some too."

For Chinese family businesses entering a new phase of succession, the transition may involve more than preserving an existing business model or transferring ownership from one generation to another due to changing markets and technologies reshaping how companies are organized and run. The next generation is also deciding how to manage capital, define ownership, and determine which aspects of a family business to carry forward.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: AI Innovation, Global Partnerships Are Hot Topics at 2026 Zhangjiang Pharma Valley Conference, BioShanghai Week
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 18 -- The 2026 Zhangjiang Pharma Valley Conference and Shanghai International Biopharmaceutical Industry Week, or BioShanghai Week for short, has opened in Shanghai, highlighting global partnerships and artificial intelligence-driven innovation.

Themed ‘AI-Driven Innovation, Building a Global Health Community,’ the four-day event kicked off yesterday and will run through Sept. 20. It brings together government officials, executives, scientists, and investors from China and abroad to discuss innovation integration, clinical transformation, capital empowerment, ecological services, collaboration among medical institutions, and global partnership.

BioShanghai Week was rebranded this year for its sixth edition, introducing a new name. It was co-organized by Shanghai Zhangjiang Pharma Valley Ecosystem Technology Development and Yicai Global’s sister company Shanghai Yicai Wanxiang Information Technology.

Li Zheng, member of the Shanghai Municipal Party Committee Standing Committee and secretary-general of the Communist Party of China Pudong New Area Committee, and Yang Sheng, deputy director of China's National Medical Products Administration, addressed the opening ceremony along with Jane Wall, director general of the UK BioIndustry Association.

China has approved 59 innovative drugs so far this year, Yang said. Of them, Shanghai had approved six domestically developed Class 1 innovative drugs as of Sept. 4, according to data disclosed at the event. The city's biopharmaceutical manufacturing output reached CNY138.2 billion (USD20.6 billion) in the first eight months of the year.

Two platforms were launched at the opening ceremony. One is a Shanghai-London life sciences partnership involving Zhangjiang Group and other institutions, such as Imperial College London and Oxford University Innovation; the other is a financing initiative bringing together domestic and international investors, including Shanghai Industrial Investment, CBC Group, and Hillhouse Capital, to support biopharma companies across their full lifecycle.

Growing Role of Chinese innovation

China accounted for around 30 percent of the global pharmaceutical pipeline last year, up from just 2 percent in 2015, Allan Gabor, operating partner at Advent International and former President of Merck China and EVP Merck Electronics, said at BioShanghai Week, citing McKinsey data. This shift has changed how multinational companies seek partnerships in China, he noted.

However, Gabor warned that a pipeline is not a promise, explaining that innovation should be measured by patient outcomes and affordability rather than approval volume alone.

Carvykti, a Chinese cell therapy developed through international collaboration, is an example of science translating into patient benefit, Gabor said, calling for closer coordination on regulatory approval, financing, and clinical readiness to close gaps in patient access, including in Southeast Asia and Africa.

Chinese biopharmaceutical assets have continued to draw international capital, said John Arbuckle, global co-head of biopharma mergers and acquisitions at J.P. Morgan. In the first half of the year, Chinese drugmakers signed about 100 cross-border deals worth about USD100 billion, with USD5 billion in upfront payments. Last year, they signed 158 deals worth USD136 billion.

Platform deals, such as those involving AstraZeneca and CSPC Pharmaceutical Group, or Pfizer and Innovent Biologics, have become more common, Arbuckle noted, adding that deal activity has grown beyond oncology into areas including neurology and women's health.

From a modality perspective, small molecules, antibodies, and antibody-drug conjugates have expanded meaningfully into polypeptides, fusion proteins, and oligos, he pointed out. “China is no longer 'me-too,' 'me-different,’ or 'me-better’ -- we are starting to see truly innovative science.”

AI Integration

AI was featured prominently in panel discussions, with executives disclosing both progress and remaining obstacles.

Translating AI-designed molecules into physical compounds remains a bottleneck, particularly for complex small molecules and cyclic peptides, said Zhang Peng, biopharmaceutical general manager at Beijing Deep Potential Technology. He called for closer integration between computational models and automated laboratories.

Organizational trust by employees and scientists in AI-generated results is the main challenge enterprises face in terms of adoption, said Tang Fei, head of information technology and AI at Hutchmed.

Meanwhile, Rosie Rodriguez, president of growth at London-based Relation Therapeutics, said pharmaceutical research and development still often runs wet-lab and computational work in parallel rather than as a continuous feedback loop.

Shanghai Strengthens Access to Innovative Treatments

Shanghai is working to facilitate the clinical adoption of innovative drugs and medical devices by improving hospital access and payment mechanisms.

Hospitals must ensure that innovative products can enter their facilities without restrictions based on drug quotas or drug-to-medical-consumable ratios, said Zhang Chao, deputy director of the Shanghai Municipal Healthcare Security Administration.

Medical institutions must convene pharmacy committee meetings within one month after the implementation of national reimbursement drug and emerging medical device lists, ensuring that eligible products are stocked, Zhang noted. Shanghai's medical insurance payments for innovative products totaled nearly CNY20 billion (USD3 billion) in 2024 and 2025 combined, he added.

Shanghai is also expanding commercial insurance products, such as the Shanghai Huibao, to complement its basic medical insurance system, as part of a broader effort to diversify payment channels for innovative treatments.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: First Singapore Cultural Festival Opens in Shanghai
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 18 -- The inaugural Singapore Cultural Festival, organized by Singaporean Chinese-language newspaper Lianhe Zaobao, kicked off in Shanghai, presenting the Southeast Asian country's diverse culture through music, films, food, cultural talks, and digital exhibitions to local audiences.

Singapore and China have deep ties and cooperate across multiple areas, Edwin Tong, culture, community, and youth minister and second minister for education of Singapore, said during the festival's opening ceremony yesterday. While a government-to-government alliance is important, the connection between the peoples of the two countries forms the foundation of their friendship, he stressed.

Cultural exchanges can help Singaporeans and Chinese people better understand how their respective cultures have evolved amid different historical and social backgrounds, while strengthening appreciation of each other's cultural heritage, he pointed out.

Public events for the festival will be held in Shanghai tomorrow and on Sept. 20, before moving to Beijing from Sept. 24 to 26. The first stop includes the Harmonic Echoes concert, jointly presented by Singapore's Siong Leng Musical Association and cross-ethnic ensemble Artusik, and the screening of four Singaporean movies -- Anthony Chen's We Are All Strangers, as well as Ajoomma, Ah Girl, and 667.

"We hope that through the festival, our Chinese friends can experience the essence of Singapore's Chinese culture, which has a unique and multiethnic character," Tong said.

The Harmonic Echoes concert is based on Nanyin, a traditional music form from Fujian, and incorporates elements of Indian classical music, while Artusik combines Malay, Chinese, Indian, Middle Eastern, and Western musical elements. 

The China Oriental Song and Dance Ensemble visited Singapore in 1979, before the two countries established diplomatic relations in 1990, Tong noted, adding that the Asian Civilizations Museum in Singapore is working with the Dunhuang Academy of China to stage the exhibition Dunhuang: Buddhist Art and the Silk Road.

Singaporean Chinese-language newspapers have long been involved not only in news dissemination but also in Chinese-language education and cultural heritage, said Ang Yiting, editor-in-chief of Lianhe Zaobao. The festival aims to allow Chinese audiences to "experience and understand Singapore culture from multiple perspectives and through multiple senses, and appreciate its diversity, different facets, and richness," she added.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: China’s Micro-Drama Output Soars Past 2025 Total as AI Production Booms
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 17-- China produced over 10 times more micro dramas in the first eight months of this year than in all of 2025, as artificial intelligence fuels a production boom.

From January to August, a total of 430,000 micro dramas, short serialized shows typically lasting just a few minutes per episode, were released nationwide, 13 times the number for the whole of last year, according to fresh data from the National Radio and Television Administration. AI-generated dramas accounted for more than 90 percent of the new titles.

The market has grown rapidly. Chinese micro dramas now reach more than 800 million users, or more than half of the country’s population. The country's micro-drama market exceeded CNY100 billion (USD14.9 billion) in 2025, when the number of users was nearly 700 million, according to data the media regulator released at a press conference in February.

AI technology has opened up new possibilities for innovative expression, lower costs, and greater efficiency in micro-drama production, but has also created new challenges for content quality and rights protection, Wang Xiaoliang, director of the administration’s Network Audiovisual Program Management Department, said at a press conference today.

Regulators will encourage innovation while strengthening oversight of AI-generated micro dramas, including requiring content labels and protecting portrait and voice rights throughout the production process, Wang said.

Regulators have made harmful and vulgar material, content unsuitable for children, and copyright infringement and piracy key targets of industry governance, Wang said. They have removed 68,000 micro dramas that violated regulations from online platforms so far this year and instructed platforms to deal with more than 1,200 accounts that broke the rules. More than 90 percent of the content removed was AI-generated, he added.

Chinese micro dramas have been shown and widely welcomed in more than 200 countries and regions and account for over 80 percent of the overseas micro-drama market, He Biao, spokesperson of the NRTA, said at the press conference.

China should make good use of the new growth engine provided by AI technology, continue consolidating the leading position of its micro-drama industry, and help Chinese micro dramas reach more overseas markets, Wang added.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Emmi Laine

data.title: Tesla Offers Up to USD1,940 Incentive to Chinese Buyers Amid September Discount Rush
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 7 -- US electric vehicle giant Tesla has joined a new round of price cuts in China's auto market, offering buyers temporary subsidies of up to CNY13,000 (USD1,940) that bring purchase costs to record lows.

Buyers who order and take delivery of Model 3 and Model Y vehicles by Sept. 30 can receive cash rewards of CNY5,000 and CNY10,000 (USD745 and USD1,490), respectively, while buyers of designated Model 3 versions can get an additional CNY8,000 insurance subsidy, Tesla China announced today.

After the incentives, the lowest prices of the Model 3 and Model Y in China have fallen to CNY222,500 and CNY253,500 (USD33,150 and USD37,770), respectively, their lowest since the refreshed versions of the two models were launched, Tesla noted.

The move comes as more than 10 automakers have rolled out promotions in China since the start of September, including options packages, cash subsidies, and preferential financing, amid sluggish demand in the world's largest auto market.

Electric vehicle maker Leapmotor Technology, for example, launched purchase benefits worth up to CNY19,680 on Sept. 1, including complimentary interior and exterior options and charging stations. Geely Auto-backed Zeekr recently offered a CNY10,000 insurance subsidy as well as financing and options discounts for its flagship Zeekr 8X sports utility vehicle.

Luxury gasoline-powered car brands have introduced even steeper discounts. SAIC Audi recently announced limited-time September prices of CNY262,800 for its A7L luxury four-door coupe and CNY467,600 for its Q6 SUV -- discounts of 37 percent and 29 percent respectively off their official guide prices.

The latest round of price cuts comes against a backdrop of weakness in China's auto market this year. Retail sales of passenger cars fell 20 percent from a year earlier to 11.8 million units in the first eight months, while retail sales of new energy vehicles dropped 11 percent to 6.7 million units, according to the latest data from the China Passenger Car Association.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Emmi Laine

data.title: Chinese Chipmaker D-Robotics Bags USD400 Million in Latest Fundraiser Led by Mirea Asset
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 17 -- D-Robotics, a Chinese robotics chip startup spun off from autonomous-driving chipmaker Horizon Robotics, has secured USD400 million in its latest funding round led by South Korean investment firm Mirae Asset Management. The proceeds will be used to strengthen its chip and software businesses and support the development of the robotics industry.

Other participants in the Series C round included Chinese on-demand services giant Meituan as well as several government-backed investment platforms and leading investment institutions, Shenzhen-based D-Robotics said today.

More than 10 shareholders of the firm including Hillhouse Group-backed GL Ventures, 5Y Capital and Linear Capital also increased their investments in this round, the firm added.

The proceeds will be used to expand the full range of computing capabilities offered by D-Robotics’ core Sunrise intelligent computing chips and build a software platform covering data collection, model training, simulation and validation as well as inference deployment to meet the development needs of the robotics industry across a range of scenarios, D-Robotics said.

D-Robotics was formerly the robotics division of Horizon Robotics before being spun off as an independent company in January 2024 to focus on the development of robotics chips. The firm has since launched three mass-produced chips, namely Sunrise 3, Sunrise 5 and Sunrise S600, along with supporting software and hardware products for robot development.

D-Robotics’ revenue jumped several times in the first half compared to the same period last year, while cumulative shipments of its Sunrise chips exceeded 8 million units, the company said. Since its launch in November last year, the Sunrise S600 has been adopted by over 20 robot manufacturers, including Tars Robot, Spirit AI and X Square, it added.

D-Robotics had completed two rounds of financing before this round, raising USD270 million in a Series B round in April and USD100 million in a Series A round in May last year.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: China Orders Country’s Largest NEV Recall Over Door Handle Safety
data.description:
(Yicai) Aug. 24 -- China has ordered the country’s biggest recall of new energy vehicles, with nine automakers -- including Tesla -- set to bring in more than 4.2 million cars because of safety concerns over concealed door handles.

The callback, ordered by the State Administration for Market Regulation on Aug. 21, is also China’s biggest cross‑brand recall stemming from a single design issue.

The carmakers involved issued recall notices the same day, citing concerns that emergency mechanical door releases in the cars blend into the interior trim, making them hard to identify and operate. In extreme situations, such as severe crashes that cause the car’s 12‑volt power supply to fail, the issue could prevent occupants from quickly opening the doors and escaping, while also making it harder for emergency crews to access the vehicle from outside.

Tesla accounts for the largest share of the recall at nearly 2.98 million cars. The vehicles were manufactured between March 2019 and late April 2026, and include both China-made and imported models. The affected lineup includes the Model 3, Model Y, Model X and Model S.

Others with sizeable callbacks include Xiaomi with 390,500, Leapmotor with 371,200, Xpeng with 264,800, and Geely Holding with 92,658.

The companies are taking different approaches to address the issue, all provided free of charge. They include placing warning labels next to the emergency mechanical releases, using over‑the‑air software updates to enable the windows to automatically lower following an accident, thereby providing an additional escape route, and replacing the handle covers to make them more visible.

China’s national standards for automotive door handles will take effect next Jan. 1. Safety hazards associated with hidden door handles have become increasingly clear, an expert told Yicai. Even though the new mandatory standards will not apply retroactively to cars already on the road, it is reasonable for automakers to recall existing vehicles to address risks, the person added.

Concealed pop-out door handles were first widely introduced to passenger cars by Austin-based Tesla with the Model S. Their streamlined appearance, improved aerodynamic performance, and high-tech appeal led many Chinese NEV manufacturers to adopt the design. But as the design spread, questions around its behavior in emergencies have become harder to ignore.

If a serious accident were to disable a vehicle’s electronic door release mechanism, hidden door handles on the outside may fail to deploy automatically, making it more difficult for rescuers to get into the car. Although emergency mechanical releases are fitted inside, their low visibility and poorly differentiated covers can make them difficult to locate quickly, impeding the chances of occupants escaping after an accident.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Kim Taylor

data.title: Council for Global Brand Building Is Launched to Address Trust Gap for Chinese Firms Venturing Abroad
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 17 -- The Council for Global Brand Building was officially initiated during the World Trade Organization's Public Forum in Geneva, aiming to address the challenges faced by Chinese companies going global.

The CGBB was announced by global business and communications consultancy iMpact’s founder and Chief Executive Officer Chris Pereira yesterday. It brings together companies, universities, media organizations, professional service providers, and independent experts to answer a single question: how do capable, well-resourced Chinese brands earn lasting credibility when going global?

China’s outbound direct investment rose 8.1 percent to USD86.5 billion in the first half of the year from a year earlier, despite cross-border acquisitions having grown more selective amid heightened geopolitical uncertainties, according to the latest data from the Ministry of Commerce.

Innovation is global, but trust is local, Pereira said about the main issue troubling Chinese companies going global. They now foray into foreign markets with mature products, technologies, and supply chains, yet strong capabilities do not automatically translate into recognition, and recognition does not automatically translate into trust, he explained.

Trust remains a fundamentally local currency that has to be earned market by market through policy environment, industry partnerships, and people-to-people exchange, Pereira noted.

Broader industry conversation on this topic has been fragmented, scattered across corporate experience, academic papers, media commentary, and consulting methodologies, without a shared venue for different parties to compare notes and build on each other’s work, the organizers of CGBB said, adding that the council was founded exactly to fill this ecosystem gap.

Leadership and Founding Partner

Pereira will chair the CGBB, and Tang Weijing, partner and head of the iMpact Academy, will serve as secretary-general. Wang Xiao, a dual-PhD holder who directs executive education at Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University, joined the council as founding advisor.

Leading Chinese financial media outlet Yicai has come on board as CGBB's founding strategic partner. Its English-language platform Yicai Global will provide coverage and analysis for the council's research, while its Yicai Research Institute will contribute research expertise and analytical support to CGBB studies and reports.

The CGBB’s initial expert committee draws from branding, academia, law, and cross-border commerce, with members including Bruce Zou, senior researcher at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, Wang Bei, associate professor at the University of International Business and Economics, Yu Jian, director of the Yicai Research Institute, Michael Low, founder and director of SENSE Collective, and Sun Yanhua, partner of Grandall Law Firm.

CGBB is now accepting applications from companies, institutions, and individual experts. Members of the expert committee are selected by invitation.

Credibility Index as First CGBB Project

As its first project, the CGBB launched the Global Credibility Index, an evaluation framework under development with academic institutions, media think tanks, companies, and outside experts.

The Global Credibility Index is designed to cover consumer perception, media reputation, branding, partner relationships, regulatory and social responsibility performance, and crisis and risk management. It will also address how artificial intelligence is reshaping brand credibility.

The index will track how Chinese brands are performing on trust in international markets and give companies a benchmark for identifying their own shortcomings.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: Z.AI Gains as Chinese AI Giant Raises Revenue Forecast After USD5 Billion Financing
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 17 -- Z.AI’s shares rose after the Chinese artificial intelligence company previously known as Zhipu AI raised its annual recurring revenue forecast after announcing plans to raise about USD5 billion from a share placement and convertible bond sale.

Z.AI [HKG: 2513] closed 2.8 percent up at HKD740 (USD94.32) in Hong Kong today, after gaining 5.9 percent yesterday. The shares began trading on Jan. 8 at HKD116.20 apiece and surged 2,465 percent to a record high of HKD2,980 (USD379.95) on June 26. They have lost around 75 percent since then.

After the refinancing, Z.AI’s computing power reserves rank among the top independent Chinese AI model developers, and its computing power supply is no longer a major constraint on short-term revenue growth, the management said at an investor conference yesterday. Therefore, the Shanghai-based firm has raised its ARR guidance for the end of this year to USD3 billion from USD2.4 billion.

ARR estimates annual income based on long-term subscription contracts with users, and it is not entirely equivalent to actual annual revenue.

Z.AI launched its flagship foundation model GLM-5 in February. Afterward, demand for model calls surged, pushing the company’s computing power reserves to near depletion. As a result, it temporarily suspended sales of its main product, Coding Plan.

To address the computing power bottleneck, Z.AI completed a share placement of HKD31.4 billion (USD4 billion) in July and revealed plans in June to raise an additional CNY15 billion (USD2.2 billion) through a secondary listing on Shanghai’s Star Market.

Moreover, the company announced on Sept. 13 that it would carry out another share placement of HKD15.7 billion, which was completed yesterday, and issue about CNY20.1 billion of zero-coupon convertible bonds. These funds will be mainly used to develop the company’s next-generation model and build its computing power infrastructure.

In addition to expanding its computing power reserves, Z.AI is actively exploring new business models, such as collaborating with cloud providers to deploy its models in a managed format on cloud platforms. This approach aims to broaden the distribution channels for its models and reduce reliance on its own computing power.

Z.AI has already signed revenue-sharing agreements with several leading cloud service providers, both domestic and international. Related revenue is expected to be recognized from next month, the management team revealed during the investor conference.

Z.AI is also actively promoting its CoWork business, which integrates models into enterprise workflows as AI agents to complete complex tasks. Since the launch of GLM-5.3 in August, the order volume for Z.AI's CoWork business has exceeded CNY1 billion (USD149.1 million), with cybersecurity being the primary application scenario.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Futura Costaglione

data.title: China's Shenling Jumps After Landing USD415 Million Order for Air Cooling Equipment
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 17 -- Shares of Shenling Environmental Systems rose after the leading Chinese air conditioner and temperature control equipment supplier said it has secured an order worth USD415 million for air cooling gear from an overseas client. 

Shenling [SHE: 301018] closed up 2.8 percent at CNY104.14 (USD15.53) a share in Shenzhen today, after earlier surging by as much as 9.1 percent. The ChiNext Index fell 0.4 percent amid mild selloff pressure after the US Federal Reserve's overnight rate hike.

Shenling signed the deal with the buyer yesterday, agreeing to deliver the equipment within 120 days, the Shunde-based company announced today. The order would build on the pair's existing collaboration by strengthening their ties, it added.

The agreement includes conditions on product names, supply quantities, unit prices, and payment terms, Shenling noted, without disclosing the client's name or further details due to commercial confidentiality. 

The deal will play a significant role in expanding Shenling's overseas presence and advancing its strategic development goals, the company said, adding that it will likely positively impact financial performance next year.

Shenling's operating revenue reached almost CNY1.8 billion (USD268.4 million) in the six months ended June 30. In comparison, the figure topped CNY4.2 billion last year.

Shenling provides temperature control solutions for computing centers, industrial applications, nuclear power, rail transit, and public buildings, holding a leading position in China's liquid cooling data center market, particularly with its coolant distribution units and their applications in the intelligent computing industry. It counts Huawei Technologies, ByteDance, Tencent Holdings, Alibaba Group Holding, Baidu, Meituan, Kuaishou Technology, and JD.Com among its clients, according to its first-half earnings report.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: Chinese LLMs Top US Rivals in Call Volume on OpenRouter for 20th Straight Week
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 17 -- The combined weekly call volume of Chinese large language models exceeded that of US models on application programming interface aggregation platform OpenRouter for the 20th week in a row despite lacking in intelligent capabilities.

Global LLM call volume on OpenRouter reached 127 trillion tokens from Sept. 7 to 13, with Chinese models accounting for nearly 61.2 trillion tokens, compared with 21.8 trillion tokens for their US rivals, according to the latest data released by the platform. The figure for Chinese LLMs rose 7.9 percent week on week, while that for US models surged 32 percent.

GPT-5.6 Luna from US developer OpenAI ranked first with 18.2 trillion, followed by Hy4 preview with 16.8 trillion and GLM-5.3-Flash with 11.9 trillion by China’s Tencent Holdings and Z.AI. Other Chinese models in the top 10 included DeepSeek’s V4-Flash-0731, V4.1-Flash, and V4-Flash-0423, which ranked fourth, sixth, and seventh, respectively, as well as Xiaomi’s MiMo-V2.5 in fifth.

DeepSeek’s V4.1 Flash processed about one trillion tokens within 24 hours of its Sept. 10 release. “It’s interesting that it just took AI users hours rather than days to use DeepSeek’s new model with their workflows and applications,” a developer pointed out.

LLMs used to be upgraded yearly, then every few months, and now almost every week. Seven leading global developers upgraded their models between Sept. 1 and Sept. 11, including US’ Anthropic launching Claude Fable 5.1 and OpenAI releasing its flagship model GPT-6 Astra.

After the latest round of upgrades, the global LLM competitive landscape shows two distinct characteristics, according to OpenRouter. In terms of capabilities, Chinese developers still miss the top five, with only Z.AI and Moonshot AI making the top 10. However, seven Chinese models rank in the top 10 by call volume, up from only two a year ago.

Chinese models are not leading in technological capabilities but have become the choice of more and more developers. Amid AI’s large-scale implementation, enterprises and users are gradually shifting their focus from capabilities to higher input-output ratios, with “Token ROI” becoming a key term in discussions, Xiong Wei, an internet industry analyst at UBS Securities in China, told Yicai at a recent exchange event.

After a round of price increases and drops, DeepSeek still plays the role of a “price butcher” in the global LLM market. About 90 percent of V4.1-Flash’s call volume comes from cache reads, the cost of which is around 0.6 US cents per million tokens based on market pricing, about 80 percent lower than similar models such as GLM-5.3-Flash, OpenRouter noted.

“Chinese models are already capable of doing most tasks of the application layer,” the developers of GitHub’s open-source project Xiaobei told Yicai, adding that unless a task is complex at the underlying level, there is no need to pay tens of times the cost for top models.

Speaking with overseas investors, Xiong said he has found that some of the world’s leading information technology companies have begun to consider incorporating Chinese open-source models into their workflows. The trend significantly accelerated from May to June, with more and more companies and developers starting to use such models to build workflows or perform specific tasks, he noted.

In addition, although Chinese model developers offer higher cost-effectiveness, they are not paying to boost adoption of their models, according to a UBS survey. Their gross profit margin is mostly in the range of 20 percent to 40 percent, meaning that they improve profitability and maintain cost-effectiveness through innovative model architecture, optimized training, and inference efficiency, the findings showed.

Editor: Martin Kadiev
